haiku-low.q1: After the Message Store commit, before any recipient is reached. The ack carries msg_id and seq, and does not wait for recipients.
haiku-low.q2: Sender gets an error. Nothing is stored and no one receives it. The retry must carry the same msg_id, so no second copy is created.
haiku-low.q3: 30 seconds after its last heartbeat, when the Presence Registry entry expires. Heartbeats are sent every 10 seconds.
haiku-low.q4: The message goes to the recipient's Offline Inbox and a push is sent. A late ack later removes the inbox entry, and repeats are dropped by msg_id.
haiku-low.q5: Nothing is retried. The Offline Inbox entry stays, so the client still gets the message on reconnect.
haiku-low.q6: Sync sends missed messages from the Offline Inbox in seq order within each conversation. The client drops duplicates by msg_id.
haiku-low.q7: The outbox row, written in the same transaction as the message, stays unpublished after a crash. The Outbox Relay publishes it later, so fan-out still happens.
haiku-low.q8: The Presence Registry holds online state. Which gateway node is recorded is NOT STATED. An entry expires 30 seconds after the last heartbeat.
haiku-low.q9: The Fan-out Worker sends it through the gateway to the open connection. The client's ack within 5 seconds confirms arrival.
haiku-low.q10: The Offline Inbox, a per-user list. Written when the recipient is offline or silent for 5 seconds. Removed by that message's ack.
haiku-low.q11: The user's Offline Inbox, then the messages it references, loaded from the Message Store.
haiku-low.q12: The event is not marked done, so the bus redelivers it. Some recipients may get the message twice, and clients drop duplicates.

sonnet.q1: After the Message Store transaction (message, seq, outbox row) commits. The ack(msg_id, seq) confirms the message is durably stored with its seq; it does not wait for or confirm any recipient delivery.
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error. Nothing is stored and no one receives anything. The retry must carry the same msg_id.
sonnet.q3: 30 seconds after their last heartbeat (heartbeats are sent every 10 seconds), when the Presence Registry entry expires.
sonnet.q4: The message goes to that user's Offline Inbox and a push is sent. The user stays online for later messages. A late ack removes the inbox entry, and a repeat delivery is dropped by msg_id.
sonnet.q5: Nothing. Push is best effort and is never retried. The inbox entry stays, so the client still gets the message on reconnect; push results never change the Offline Inbox or Message Store.
sonnet.q6: In seq order within each conversation. The client drops any duplicate by msg_id.
sonnet.q7: The outbox row is written in the same transaction as the message, so it persists. If the process crashes before publishing, the row stays unpublished and the Outbox Relay publishes it later, so fan-out still happens.
sonnet.q8: In the Presence Registry. It records which users are online; the entry expires 30 seconds after the last heartbeat, so heartbeats stopping removes it. NOT STATED whether it records which gateway node a user is on.
sonnet.q9: The Fan-out Worker checks the Presence Registry, and if the user is online sends the message through the gateway to the client over its WebSocket. The client's ack, which must arrive within 5 seconds, confirms arrival.
sonnet.q10: In the Offline Inbox, a per-user list with one entry per undelivered message holding a reference to the message in the Message Store. It is written by the Fan-out Worker when a recipient is offline or does not ack within 5 seconds. An entry is removed by any ack for that message, or expires after 30 days.
sonnet.q11: The gateway reads the user's Offline Inbox, then loads those messages from the Message Store and sends them.
sonnet.q12: The event is not marked done, so the Event Bus redelivers it until the worker finishes. Some recipients may get the message twice, and clients drop duplicates by msg_id.
